title: Sins of the Detective — Part 2
summary: The suspected killer from the previous episode is found stabbed after a heated argument with Neville. Neville is arrested and another DI is brought on the case to investigate.
method: The killer followed Neville to the professor's hotel and waited for Neville to leave before stabbing the professor. A decoy key was left in the room, giving the illusion of a locked room when it wasn't. They later swapped back the keys at the station.
motive: Neville had put the killer's sister in jail back in Manchester, and she later committed suicide. The killer holds Neville responsible because he didn't do the proper investigation to realize it was actually the killer, not the sister, who was a career criminal.
notes:
It is interesting how the Neville/Sophie story has a lot of parallels with the Humphrey/Martha story (they're from the same city, they meet when one of them is on holiday)
The story has never made sense to me. Why would Neville go alone to confront the suspect when he usually brings the team with him? Why would he have an argument with him in a hotel where one entrance is conveniently not covered by CCTV? Why did Sophie even target Neville when it was his friend Andrew who turned out to be a crooked cop? She was too scared to take the fall for her sister but yet she blames Neville for not investigating? And why go through the trouble of finding him in Saint Marie and pretending to date him? Why not target Andrew who was back home in Manchester?
